media.title: The Velvet Queen
media.plot: Wildlife photographer Vincent Munier takes writer Sylvain Tesson to the Tibetan plateau to photograph the elusive snow leopard.

media.title: Planet Earth II - Mountains
media.plot: Landmark footage captures a snow leopard hunting on impossible Himalayan cliffs, revealing behaviors never before filmed.

media.title: Snow Leopard: Beyond the Myth
media.plot: A team of researchers tracks snow leopards through the mountains of Pakistan using camera traps and radio collars.

media.title: Frozen Planet II
media.plot: Features the snow leopard navigating increasingly unpredictable mountain weather as climate change reshapes its alpine habitat.

habitat.description: The snow leopard inhabits the rugged mountain ranges of Central Asia, from 3,000 to 5,500 meters in altitude. These solitary cats traverse steep, rocky terrain with extraordinary agility, using their long tails for balance. They prefer broken terrain, cliffs, and ravines that provide cover for ambush hunting.

threats.name: Climate Change
threats.description: Rising temperatures push the treeline higher, shrinking the alpine zone snow leopards depend upon and fragmenting remaining habitat.

threats.name: Retaliatory Killing
threats.description: Herders kill snow leopards in retaliation for livestock predation, particularly in areas where wild prey has been depleted.

threats.name: Poaching
threats.description: Pelts and bones are trafficked illegally, and prey species like blue sheep and ibex are overhunted.

threats.name: Mining and Infrastructure
threats.description: Mining operations and road construction in mountain passes fragment habitat and increase human disturbance.

keyPrograms: Global Snow Leopard & Ecosystem Protection Program

culturalSignificance.overview: Known as the 'Ghost of the Mountains,' the snow leopard embodies the mystique of Central Asia's highest peaks. Rarely seen by humans, it has inspired reverence among the pastoral communities who share its mountain home for millennia.
literature: The Snow Leopard by Peter Matthiessen
The Velvet Queen by Sylvain Tesson
culturalSignificance.symbolism: Represents elusiveness, spiritual solitude, and the untouched wilderness of high mountains. A metaphor for nature's most hidden treasures.
